findings.highlight: Rider must be nearby, protecting Sakura
findings.evidenceJa: ライダーは潜んでいて、今も桜を守っているんだろうか
findings.governingReading: Shirou wonders whether Rider is concealed nearby and still guarding Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English promotes Shirou’s open question into certainty.

findings.highlight: I have to go introduce myself to her properly
findings.evidenceJa: ちゃんと話しておかないと
findings.governingReading: Shirou needs to speak matters through properly with Rider.
findings.explanation: The English reduces a substantive coordination talk to a social introduction.

findings.highlight: The figure seems to be waiting for my reaction
findings.evidenceJa: 人影は廊下で、こちらの出方を窺っている
findings.governingReading: The figure waits in the corridor, watching to see how Shirou will respond.
findings.explanation: The English omits the figure’s hallway position.

findings.evidenceJa: 跳び退こうとした腰を落とす
findings.governingReading: Shirou lowers the hips he had raised to spring away.
findings.explanation: The English removes the aborted evasive action and makes the movement ordinary sitting.

findings.evidenceJa: 艶やかなだけでなく、どこかおかしい
findings.governingReading: Sakura is not merely alluring or sensual; something about her is also strange.
findings.explanation: The English omits the alluring quality Shirou first notices, leaving “something else” without its first term.
The dangerous direction of Sakura’s fall disappears.

findings.highlight: a poison made by human hands
findings.evidenceJa: 人の手による毒ではないのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou wonders whether the cause is human-administered poison rather than illness.
findings.explanation: The English promotes Shirou’s hypothesis into a factual diagnosis.

findings.highlight: I just wanted to be with you
findings.governingReading: Shirou was the one who wanted Sakura to remain there with him.
findings.explanation: The English shifts the focus from Sakura’s continued presence to Shirou’s desire to accompany her.

findings.highlight: It’s not the voice of someone feverish
findings.evidenceJa: 高熱にうなされて、朦朧としているみたいな正体のない声
findings.governingReading: An insubstantial voice as though Sakura is delirious and dazed by high fever.
findings.explanation: The English directly reverses the comparison and says the voice is not feverish.

findings.highlight: Sakura is clinging tightly to me
findings.evidenceJa: 血が滲むほど俺を握りしめる桜
findings.governingReading: Sakura grips Shirou so hard that blood seeps out.
findings.explanation: The English omits the grip’s injurious force and blood.

findings.evidenceJa: 温かい唇が、救いを求めるように指を噛む
findings.governingReading: Sakura’s warm lips bite Shirou’s finger as though seeking salvation.
findings.explanation: The English omits the lips and their warmth from the startling physical contact.

findings.highlight: pain and blood begin to pour out from the inside
findings.evidenceJa: 内側からじわじわと痛みと血が湧き出してくる
findings.governingReading: Pain and blood gradually well up from beneath the broken skin.
findings.explanation: The English replaces gradual internal welling with blood pouring out.

findings.evidenceJa: 頼りなさが残っている
findings.governingReading: Sakura has calmed, but a lingering physical frailty or precariousness remains.
findings.explanation: The English converts residual weakness into a sad-looking emotional expression.

findings.highlight: In this silence, it makes a very definitive answer
findings.evidenceJa: 沈黙は時に、どうしようもないほどの肯定になる
findings.governingReading: Silence can sometimes amount to an affirmation so absolute that nothing can be done about it.
findings.explanation: The English is grammatically malformed and weakens the force of Sakura’s silence as an unavoidable affirmation.

findings.highlight: I just wanted to love you so I’d be able to drink your blood
findings.evidenceJa: 先輩の血が飲めるから好きになれば良いんじゃないかって
findings.governingReading: Sakura fears that perhaps she could simply call it love because loving Shirou would give her access to his blood.
findings.explanation: The English reverses the suspected motive, making blood drinking the goal of wanting to love him rather than the benefit that may have produced the supposed love.

findings.highlight: I don’t even know why I should have to say it
findings.evidenceJa: 何故そんな事を言われるのか、判らない
findings.governingReading: Shirou cannot understand why Sakura is saying such a thing to him.
findings.explanation: The English assigns the speech problem to Shirou and changes being told something into having to say it himself.

findings.highlight: I pat Sakura on the back
findings.governingReading: Shirou lightly pats Sakura’s shoulder to encourage her.
findings.explanation: The English relocates the touch from her shoulder to her back.

findings.highlight: I’m being eaten by something strange
findings.evidenceJa: よく分からない何かに食いつかれ
findings.governingReading: Something incomprehensible has bitten or latched onto Shirou.
findings.explanation: The English changes a localized clinging bite into the broader claim that the creature is eating him.
